static_traits.name: Lin Feng
static_traits.family_status: Lives with family; has a best friend Calden
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy; without significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and scenes concretely; highly cooperative, positive attitude; presenting catastrophizing and black-and-white cognitive styles when describing the future and competition results

basic_info.main_problem: Received a rejection letter from a gifted program, making me feel that all my efforts in soccer would be meaningless.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these disappointments and stress are affecting my enjoyment of football and my overall mood.
growth_experiences: After receiving a rejection letter from a gifted program, her mood was markedly affected: she said she had invested a lot of time and energy in the program, and felt highly pressured upon receiving the rejection; since then, thoughts like 'if I do not win, practice is meaningless' appeared in soccer; academic performance affected; her relationship with her best friend Calden grew tense as she focused more on disappointment; low mood and decreased drive; every loss or thought of the rejection letter re-triggers disappointment and stress.

core_beliefs: Only winning or being selected makes effort worthwhile
Failure means my future will be terrible and all efforts wasted

special_situations.event: Received a rejection letter from a gifted program
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been selected, it means I am not good enough and past efforts were all wasted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proves themselves by practicing more and forcing themselves to work harder; avoids sharing feelings with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed; all my efforts were meaningless

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If we have not won, all practice is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overtraining, evaluating performance by all-or-nothing standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Losing means I am no good; practice is utterly worthless

special_situations.event: On lonely nights thinking about long-term goals, finances, and retirement
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The future is uncontrollable and likely headed for a bad outcome (loneliness and financial instability)
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distracting attention by watching TV or reading, avoiding continued thinking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely be lonely and financially unstable when retired

special_situations.event: Thinking about the economic climate and examples of others' retirement struggles
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Seeing negative cases makes me think my future will be just as bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Selectively focuses on negative information, ignoring positive factors such as existing savings and family support
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The economy will worsen, and I too will fall into hardship in retirement

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and to prove the meaning of effort through success, while obtaining a sense of security of stability and connection
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated after failure, becoming lonely and financially insecure, with efforts proven utterly meaningless
defense_goal: Tries to control outcomes and avoid the sense of failure by practicing doubly hard
Reducing anxiety about the future through distraction and avoidance

object_relations.self_representation: A disappointed person after rejection, worrying about disappointing others and not expressing emotions
object_relations.object_representation: Important others (e.g. friends) are presumed to be people who may not understand or may judge her

object_relations.self_representation: A team member who must prove his worth by winning
object_relations.object_representation: The team and others, like judges, measure worth by outcomes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on the future, retirement, and finances
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to see discussions of the future as triggering uncontrollable bad outcomes, using rational analysis of finances and savings to dilute emotions (transference: covering emotions with rationality)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle and empathic tone, first accurately reflecting her fear and worries, then inviting her to describe bodily sensations and present emotions; reducing interpretation, using open-ended questions to guide concretization and present-moment experience.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When losing or when negative images are repeatedly activated on lonely nights
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that staying with feelings will make her lose control, thus turning to distracting activities to avoid discomfort (transference: seeing discussion as a threat)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintaining a steady, slow pace, naming her distraction pattern, inviting her to briefly stay with the core discomfort (30-60 seconds), using grounding exercises and breathing, guiding attention back to the present moment.

manifestations: Feeling 'all effort is wasted' after receiving a rejection letter
Envisioning a lonely post-retirement life with no one to talk to
Not yet sharing true feelings with best friend Calden
outcomes: Avoiding deep communication leads to relationship tension

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Evaluates self-worth by the rule of 'must win / must practice more'
Treats the outcome (winning / being admitted) as the only standard

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on
manifestations: Using TV or reading to distract herself when alone, avoiding facing strong anxiety about the future
Shifts from core emotions to topical, situational narration

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Not expressing true feelings and stress to best friend Calden
Internalizing emotions and handling disappointment through self-pressure (extra practice)

positive_force: Having some savings and good family relationships as potential support
Has a best friend Calden who can serve as a support resource
Proactively seeks help, positive attitude, willing to do cognitive restructuring and record thoughts
Has tendencies toward effort and self-discipline (extra practice in soccer)
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases: catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering, and predicting the future
Excessively focusing on disappointment and negative prospects, ignoring positive evidence and support
Short-term relief through distraction avoidance but maintains the problem cycle
Emotions and needs not yet expressed; support system not yet activated
Stress affects studies and relationships; motivation and enjoyment decline

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing about the future and avoiding through distraction (TV/reading) when alone
antecedent: Thinking about long-term goals or financial and retirement plans
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong disappointment and stress formed after receiving the gifted-program rejection letter, triggering pessimistic anticipation and catastrophic thinking about the future
target_behavior.function: Escaping anxiety and discomfort, gaining short-term emotional relief and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased attention, anxiety keeps returning; affecting focus on daily tasks and social interaction

target_behavior.behavior: Evaluating herself by all-or-nothing standards after losing, with 'practice is meaningless' thoughts or compulsive overtraining
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'only winning is valuable' and black-and-white thinking drive results-oriented self-evaluation
target_behavior.function: Tries to restore a sense of control and avoid the shame / disappointment brought by failure
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment, increased stress; tense relationships with friends, overall low mood and impaired motivation
